characterization_methods.key_findings: YS ~900 MPa and UTS ~1000 MPa at 8Al for the 550 °C/24 h condition
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and total elongation

characterization_methods.key_findings: ~375 HBW at 8Al for the 550 °C/24 h condition

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size (hot-rolled/water-quenched state)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sections perpendicular to rolling direction; grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Prevalent deformation mechanism consists of Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods and subsequent expansion of dislocation loops, assisted by dislocation cross-slip and, to a minor extent, shearing of κ-carbides.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging at 550 °C for 24 h promotes formation of nm-sized κ-carbides and pronounced strengthening.

phase_interfaces.coherence: lattice mismatch below 3% with austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix (enables cuboidal coherent nanoprecipitates)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Strain hardening after aging at 500–600 °C is dominated by κ-carbide strengthening (Orowan bypassing of κ-carbide rods) rather than mechanical twinning.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: YS, UTS, hardness, and ductility after 24 h aging
comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: YS, UTS, and hardness increased to levels twice as high as the as-homogenized state; ductility drastically reduced

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise in the furnace; successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.
Aging conducted in air at 550 °C for 24 h followed by oil quenching.
Scales removed from surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens from 2 mm thick sheet segments (2×60×55 mm³)

precipitates.coherency: lattice mismatch below 3% with the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix (cuboidal nanoprecipitates)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic (γ, fcc) matrix with nm-sized κ-carbide (L′1₂) precipitates after aging at 550 °C for 24 h

unmapped_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 24 h increases YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as in the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility (opposite trend to the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy).

The specific total elongation (TE) for the 550 °C/24 h condition at 8 wt.% Al is not separately reported in Fig. 3c; at 8Al, TE falls to near 10% for the sibling 500 °C/24 h and 600 °C/24 h conditions.

The strengthening is attributed to formation of nm-sized κ-carbides during aging; the paper additionally states (in the context of Fig. 5, aged at 600 °C) that these κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h with only modest coarsening.
